title: What If the Biggest Solar Storm Ever Recorded Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if the 1859 solar storm hit today? Back then it only made telegraph machines spark.
In 1859 auroras glowed as far south as Cuba and Panama. In Missouri, people could read by the light after midnight.
Today the wires are power grids. Storm currents could damage huge transformers, and some take a year or more to replace.
GPS, radio and satellites in low orbit would be disrupted too.
A 2017 study put a severe blackout across two thirds of the United States at about forty billion dollars a day.
Storms like it can strike again. The only question is whether the grid is ready when one does.
